label: copy phase of length-3 sequences (strongest on the final copy step)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never during the original tokens or on <DEL>. Its core is length-3 sequences: about 30% of L=3 copy steps are active vs about 1% overall, and they hold about 64% of activation mass. Within L=3 the last copy step (t=5, outputting orig(2)) is active ~98% of the time and carries the largest values (top activations are all there, often with input p). The t=4 step is weaker (~79%). The rest of the mass is a weak, scattered tail on longer sequences, mostly L=4 at the second-to-last copy step (to_go=1) and copy steps where the input is p, o, h, or a digit. These have low magnitude and no clean rule. Never fires on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=1) or on recall_idx=0. Recall is incomplete (~36% of active steps) because of the long-sequence tail.
